name: workspace_stack
summary: The Loom shell as workflow_card IR. A workspace = stacked morph.engine cards in a body, where every control is categorized by its zone, object, and blast radius. The three-zone law is structural, not cosmetic: card navbar acts on one engine (view-only, no mutation), left FLOW acts on the whole body/app (semantic + structural, crosses commitment boundaries), top SYSTEMS acts on launches (observe post-commit, no edit). Mixing them is the bug — visual proximity must equal scope. Canonical shell is studio/loom/morph_engine.html.

inputs.name: stack
inputs.notes: Ordered list (top → bottom) of {name, kind, card_id}. kind ∈ {morph_engine, pipeline, scope, blend_engine, engine_morpher, leaf}

inputs.name: cascade
inputs.notes: Inter-engine evaluation flow. Bottom-up within one engine; top-down between engines.

zones.law: A control here changes which panes you see on ONE card. Geometry + data are identical after every toggle. Local, non-destructive, reversible.

controls.rationale: evaluation cutoff is a chain property; engine A's export into B can't be card-local
circle routing is a relationship BETWEEN engines (last out → first in); no engine owns it
re-lays-out the entire body; body-level not card-level
forks all engines into a new app lineage; one level above any engine
crosses PRESENT→PAST: editable → hashed/running; same temporal law as the .bb crystal chain

zones.law: Acts on relationships between engines or the app as a whole. The only zone that crosses commitment boundaries — branch creates lineage, launch hashes the body. Putting a commitment operator next to a view toggle would tell the user they're the same kind of action; they categorically are not.

controls.rationale: copies a frozen launch snapshot BACK into an editable body — the only path from post-commit to PRESENT

zones.law: Acts on launches — running things you read, never edit. A different lifecycle phase entirely. The fork action is the only escape hatch from post-commit; it re-enters PRESENT as a new lineage.

passes.notes: Every node's kind must resolve in the registry. Unknown kinds → reject with reasons[].

Categorical safety gate. Reject if (a) a control's domain doesn't match its zone's object, (b) a mutates_model=false zone declares an action that touches body/app state, (c) a commitment_boundary=true control sits outside the left_flow zone. Same shape as kernel_registry.resolve — a closed safety set.

Jinja2 template emits studio/loom/workspace_<crystal>.html. Template clones the morph_engine.html shell (top ribbon = systems, left shelf = flow, body = stacked cards, per-card cardnav = view). Zone position is structurally enforced — controls cannot leak into wrong zones.

Same composition rendered as a Godot 4 scene_tree with 3 sibling Control roots — TopRibbon (SystemsView), LeftShelf (FlowControls), BodyFeed (CardStack). Per-card view toggles live INSIDE each SubViewport so they cannot reach across to siblings.
tier='loom_composition'. Coords carry [card_count, zone_count=3, commitment_boundary_count, launch_actions_count]. The launch crystal anchored here is the body's PRESENT→PAST transition record.

layer_stack.name: body_cards
layer_stack.rationale: the body itself — the substrate the other zones act on

layer_stack.name: left_flow_zone
layer_stack.rationale: structural mutations that change body shape + lifecycle

layer_stack.name: top_systems_zone
layer_stack.rationale: post-commit overlay — observable launches above the editing surface

invariants: card_navbar.mutates_model === false (any toggle MUST be a pure view)
left_flow is the ONLY zone with commitment_boundary === true
top_systems.post_commit === true (read-only on hashed snapshots; fork is the only re-entry)
no control may declare a domain that crosses zones (e.g. card.view cannot touch body.*)
